HISTORY MODAL — UX REWORK
Three directions for the draft cheat sheet's Hist modal, in the app's real dark tokens. Same data, three ways to make the takeaway land. Pick one (or mix), and I'll build it into the live modal.

CURRENT — what ships today. Six competing numbers (58 hero, 3-up tiers, 2-up compare) with no clear hierarchy; the jargon heading "Two groups, not one chance"; and no plain-language verdict on whether he's worth the pick.

A · VERDICT-FIRST (leading candidate). Plain-English verdict on top, then ONE comparison bar with a "+17 edge" callout that replaces the confusing two-group heading. Tier ladder shrinks to a supporting strip; comps + trends collapse away. Best mix of clarity and compactness.

B · SCANNABLE (power user). Keeps everything on one screen: hero + finish-ladder bars up top, a single diverging "profile vs price" bar, and the top 3 trends inline with a "see all". Densest — for drafters who want the evidence without clicking.

C · GUIDED CARDS (friendliest / mobile). Each idea is its own titled, iconed card with big touch targets and a centered hero. Narrower, reads top-to-bottom like a story. Most whitespace, most taps to see detail.
